original_value: Rapid detection and early warning systems demonstrate crucial significance in tsunami risk reduction measures. So far, several tsunami observation networks have been deployed in tsunamigenic regions to issue effective local response. However, guidance on where to station these sensors are limited. In this article, we address the problem of determining the placement of tsunami sensors with the least possible tsunami detection time. We use the solutions of the 2D nonlinear shallow water equations to compute the wave travel time. The optimization problem is solved by implementing the particle swarm optimization algorithm. We apply our model to a simple test problem with varying depths. We also use our proposed method to determine the placement of sensors for early tsunami detection in Cotabato Trench, Philippines.

result.paraphrase: Rapid detection and early-warning systems are vital for reducing tsunami risk. Several tsunami observation networks have already been deployed in tsunamigenic regions to enable effective local response, but guidance on optimal sensor placement remains limited. This article addresses how to place tsunami sensors so as to minimize detection time. Wave travel time is computed using solutions of the 2D nonlinear shallow water equations, and the optimization problem is solved with the particle swarm optimization algorithm. The model is tested on a simple varying-depth case and then used to determine sensor placement for early tsunami detection in the Cotabato Trench, Philippines.
